title: Low Water Pressure / Fill Fault
shortDescription: Wash tank has not reached minimum fill level within the allowed fill time.
fullDescription:
Hobart AM, CLeN and FT commercial dishwashers use a pressure transducer or float switch to confirm tank fill. E1 indicates the tank did not reach operational level within the programmed fill window (typically 90-180 seconds). The cycle is blocked until the fault is resolved because running the wash pump dry will destroy the seal.

Most often caused by closed supply valves or clogged Y-strainers on the inlet. On AM15 and AM16 undercounter machines, a failed solenoid coil is also common.

causes.cause: Water supply valve closed or partly closed

fixSteps.title: Verify water supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm both hot water supply valve and any upstream backflow preventer are fully open and static pressure is 20-120 psi per the spec plate.

fixSteps.title: Clean Y-strainer
fixSteps.instruction: Close supply, remove the Y-strainer cap on the inlet, clean screen, reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Test fill solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: With power on and cycle started, measure voltage at solenoid coil. If voltage is present but no flow, replace coil/valve.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — Hobart warranty requires authorized service on steam/solenoid plumbing.
videoSearchQuery: Hobart dishwasher E1 low water pressure fix

faq.q: Can I bypass the fill sensor to run a cycle?
faq.a: No — running the wash pump dry in under 30 seconds destroys the mechanical seal.

title: Wash or Rinse Temperature Too Low
shortDescription: Tank water did not reach required wash or final-rinse temperature.
fullDescription:
Hobart machines must achieve 150F wash and 180F final rinse (or use chemical sanitize at lower temps per NSF) to sanitize. E2 fires when the tank heater or booster heater cannot reach setpoint within the timeout.

On high-temp sanitize machines, this is most often a failed booster heater element, tripped high-limit, or scaled element. On chemical sanitize models, it is frequently a failed tank heater contactor.

causes.cause: Booster heater element scaled or open

fixSteps.title: Verify incoming water temp
fixSteps.instruction: Measure inlet water temperature during fill — must be at least 110F (high-temp) or per spec plate.

fixSteps.title: Reset high-limit
fixSteps.instruction: Locate manual-reset high-limit on booster; press button. If it immediately trips again, element or thermostat is bad.

fixSteps.title: Test element
fixSteps.instruction: Power off/lock out. Measure element resistance; open = bad. Descale or replace as needed.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — high-voltage 208/240V element work.
videoSearchQuery: Hobart AM15 E2 low wash temperature

faq.a: Only if the machine is a chemical-sanitize model; high-temp models must hit 180F final rinse for NSF compliance.

title: Drain Pump Fault
shortDescription: Drain pump failed to empty the wash tank within the allowed time.
fullDescription: E3 is triggered when the tank has not drained below the low-level switch within the programmed drain period. Almost always debris in the drain pump impeller, a clogged overflow standpipe, or a kinked drain hose.

causes.cause: Food debris in drain pump impeller

symptoms: Standing water in tank at cycle end

fixSteps.title: Clear standpipe and scrap tray
fixSteps.instruction: Remove overflow tube and scrap basket; flush debris out.

fixSteps.title: Access drain pump
fixSteps.instruction: Lock out power, remove side panel, inspect impeller for bones, toothpicks, glass.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump if seized
fixSteps.instruction: If impeller is damaged or motor does not spin freely, install Hobart OEM drain pump.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech when pump removal requires breaking plumbing unions.
videoSearchQuery: Hobart E3 drain pump clog fix

faq.q: Does this mean the pump is dead?
faq.a: Usually no — 80% of E3 faults are debris. Clear the impeller first.

title: Final Rinse Flow Fault
shortDescription: Final rinse flow switch did not confirm adequate water flow during sanitizing rinse.
fullDescription:
Hobart uses a flow switch in the rinse line to confirm that clean, hot water is actually being delivered to the wash chamber during final rinse. If the switch does not close, E4 is logged and the cycle reports failure.

Causes are scale in the rinse arms, a failed rinse booster pump, or a clogged inlet to the booster.

fixSteps.title: Descale rinse arms
fixSteps.instruction: Remove upper and lower rinse arms, soak in commercial descaler, clear each nozzle.

fixSteps.title: Test flow switch
fixSteps.instruction: Access rinse plumbing, confirm switch closes under flow with meter.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — hidden plumbing.
videoSearchQuery: Hobart CLeN E4 rinse flow switch

faq.a: Yes — hard water is the primary cause of repeat E4 faults.

title: Wash Arm Rotation / Pressure Fault
shortDescription: Wash pump pressure below threshold or wash arms not rotating.
fullDescription:
E5 indicates inadequate wash pressure sensed at the wash pump outlet, or on models with rotation sensors, that wash arms are not spinning. Almost always caused by blocked wash arm jets, flatware jammed in the pump intake, or a failed pump.

Severe wash-arm obstruction will also damage plastic bearings.

fixSteps.title: Remove and inspect wash arms
fixSteps.instruction: Lift out upper/lower wash arms, clear any foreign objects, descale jets.

fixSteps.title: Clear pump intake
fixSteps.instruction: Remove pump screen and check for flatware; a single fork can stall the pump.

fixSteps.title: Test pump motor amps
fixSteps.instruction: With cover on, check motor amp draw vs nameplate; over-amp means mechanical issue inside pump.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — wash pump is plumbed to the tank with specialty seals.
videoSearchQuery: Hobart E5 wash arm wash pump fault

faq.q: Can a single fork really cause this?
faq.a: Yes — the wash pump is a high-flow centrifugal and any hard object stops it.

title: Door Switch / Hood Not Closed
shortDescription: Door safety switch not confirming that the hood or door is fully closed.
fullDescription: All commercial dishwashers require a closed-door interlock before the wash pump runs to prevent scalding. E6 indicates the interlock is open during an expected closed phase. Usually a misaligned switch or broken actuator.
symptoms: Cycle won't start with door shut

fixSteps.title: Fully close door/hood
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure door latch or hood fully seats — listen for click.

fixSteps.title: Inspect actuator
fixSteps.instruction: Open door, visually confirm actuator is not bent and switch plunger moves freely.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: If continuity fails with actuator depressed, replace switch assembly.

whenToCallPro: Usually DIY; call pro if the actuator assembly is integral to the door.

faq.q: Can I jumper the switch to test?
faq.a: Only momentarily for diagnosis — running a dishwasher with the door open is a scald hazard.

title: Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Wash tank or booster thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range.
fullDescription: E7 points to a failed or disconnected tank/booster thermistor. Without valid temperature input, the controller cannot confirm sanitizing temp and inhibits the cycle.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connector
fixSteps.instruction: Locate thermistor harness at control board, disconnect and reseat.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Drain tank, unscrew thermistor from well, install OEM replacement with thermal paste if specified.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech to drain and refill without damaging gaskets.

faq.a: If the sensor well is scaled and reading slow/low, yes — otherwise the sensor must be replaced.

title: Conveyor Jam / Drive Motor Fault (FT Series)
shortDescription: Flight-type (FT) conveyor has stalled or drive motor has tripped.
fullDescription: On Hobart FT1000/FT900 flight-type machines, E8 indicates that the conveyor drive has stalled or the overload has tripped — typically a rack jammed in the curtains, debris binding the conveyor, or a failed drive motor.

fixSteps.title: E-stop and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Hit emergency stop, open hood and clear jammed rack or debris.

fixSteps.title: Reset overload
fixSteps.instruction: At control panel, reset conveyor motor overload per service manual.

fixSteps.title: Service chain
fixSteps.instruction: Weekly: rinse flight chain and inspect for stretched links.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — flight chain alignment is critical.

faq.q: How do I prevent conveyor jams?
faq.a: Remove large debris at the pre-rinse and train staff to load flatware upright in cylinders.

title: Chemical Dispenser / Detergent Low
shortDescription: Detergent or sanitizer level switch reports empty container.
fullDescription:
E9 is reported by machines with level sensors in the detergent or sanitizer tote line. A float switch in the pickup tube indicates low product. Without detergent or sanitizer, the machine will not sanitize.

On chemical-sanitize AM15 units, this also fires when the sanitizer pump fails to prime.

fixSteps.title: Replace tote
fixSteps.instruction: Swap empty jug for full chemical supply.

fixSteps.title: Prime pump
fixSteps.instruction: Run dispenser prime function until product flows.

fixSteps.title: Replace squeeze tubing
fixSteps.instruction: Peristaltic tubing wears every 6-12 months; replace with OEM tubing.

whenToCallPro: Most chemical companies service dispensers as part of the chemical contract.

faq.a: Usually your chemical supplier (Ecolab, Auto-Chlor, etc.) includes service in the contract.

title: Control Board / Memory Fault
shortDescription: Main control board has failed self-test or lost configuration memory.
fullDescription: E0 indicates the main control board has failed EEPROM/memory self-test on boot, or has lost its configuration. Often caused by a lightning surge, water intrusion in the control box, or simple end-of-life on older boards.

fixSteps.title: Inspect enclosure
fixSteps.instruction: Check for water or steam intrusion; dry and reseal if found.

fixSteps.title: Replace control board
fixSteps.instruction: OEM replacement, re-enter configuration per service manual.

whenToCallPro: Commercial equipment often requires certified service tech — Hobart boards must be configured to the specific model/voltage.

faq.q: Is a surge protector worth it?
faq.a: Yes — commercial-grade surge protection prevents the most common E0 cause.
